course.name: Welding Technology Certification Preparation Program
course.subject: welding
course.prerequisite_policy: Open-course enrollment; prerequisites and learner eligibility may be configured by the provider.

course_learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe welding practices and OSHA compliance.
Identify welding tools, equipment, and personal protective equipment (PPE).
Explain the principles of metallurgy and metal fabrication.
Read and interpret welding symbols, blueprints, and fabrication drawings.
Perform Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW/MIG), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW/TIG), and Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) concepts.
Prepare, weld, inspect, and troubleshoot welded joints.
Understand welding codes, quality standards, and inspection procedures.
Perform basic cutting processes using oxy-fuel and plasma equipment.
Apply mathematics used in welding fabrication and layout.
Prepare for national welding certification examinations.

program_overview: Welding Technology Certification Preparation Program
24-Week Online Welding Technology Program
Learn. Weld. Inspect. Certify.
Program Summary

The Welding Technology Certification Preparation Program is a comprehensive 24-week online workforce development course designed to prepare students for careers in welding and metal fabrication while equipping them with the technical knowledge and practical skills needed to successfully complete nationally recognized welding certification examinations.
The curriculum aligns with industry expectations and prepares students for certifications and assessments offered through organizations such as:
American Welding Society (AWS) Certified Welder (CW) Program
AWS Certified Welding Inspector (Foundational Knowledge)
NCCER Welding Levels 1–4
American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Welding Standards
Employer and apprenticeship welding qualification tests

Through interactive instruction, virtual welding laboratories, welding simulations, AI-powered coaching, quizzes, module tests, and comprehensive practice examinations, students develop the competencies required to safely perform welding operations, interpret welding blueprints, inspect weld quality, troubleshoot defects, and enter the welding workforce with confidence.
Program Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of this program, students will be able to:
Demonstrate safe welding practices and OSHA compliance.
Identify welding tools, equipment, and personal protective equipment (PPE).
Explain the principles of metallurgy and metal fabrication.
Read and interpret welding symbols, blueprints, and fabrication drawings.
Perform Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW/MIG), Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW/TIG), and Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) concepts.
Prepare, weld, inspect, and troubleshoot welded joints.
Understand welding codes, quality standards, and inspection procedures.
Perform basic cutting processes using oxy-fuel and plasma equipment.
Apply mathematics used in welding fabrication and layout.
Prepare for national welding certification examinations.
Program Structure
Program Length: 24 Weeks
Delivery Format: Online, Hybrid, or Instructor-Led
Weekly Commitment: 6–8 Hours
Instructional Modules: 12 (2 Weeks Each)
Required Mastery: 80%
